text: Row-major traversal of a 4000x4000 grid measured 3x faster than column-major for identical work. Why?
choices: Memory is fetched in cache lines, so consecutive access gets many elements nearly free
The rows were shorter than the columns
explanation: Reading grid[r][0] pulls in a line containing the next fifteen or so ints; reading down a column touches a different array each time and pays full price. Walk data in the order it is stored — vary the last index innermost.
